skill.name: find-skills
skill.description: Search multiple agent skill registries from one command, compare native popularity signals, flag locally installed skills, and heuristically scan top candidates before recommending them.
skill.summary: Find and compare agent skills across skills.sh, clawhub.ai, and GitHub.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives after contextual review. The skill performs read-only registry searches, writes temporary result files, and uses grep patterns to warn about risky third-party candidates; no secret access, code execution of downloaded content, prompt injection, or destructive behavior was found.

content.value_statement: Finding the right agent skill is hard when each registry has different coverage and ranking signals. This skill searches major registries together, compares native metrics, and highlights safety signals before a recommendation.
actual_capabilities: Searches skills.sh, clawhub.ai, and GitHub skill topics from one command.
Ranks each source by its own native metric, such as installs, stars, or keyword match.
Flags skills that appear to already be installed in local skill directories.
Fetches top candidate skill files and scans them for risky patterns.
Can output either a formatted report or machine-readable JSON.
limitations: Requires curl and jq, and GitHub results need the gh CLI.
Search quality depends on registry indexing and the query terms used.
The security scan is heuristic and is not a full audit.
It does not install skills automatically.

use_cases.title: Recommend an existing skill
use_cases.description: Search registries before building a custom workflow, then recommend one primary skill with evidence.

use_cases.title: Compare marketplace coverage
use_cases.description: Check skills.sh, clawhub.ai, and GitHub for the same need without relying on one leaderboard.

use_cases.title: Screen candidate skills before use
use_cases.description: Identify risky installation or secret-access patterns in top candidates before sharing them with a user.

prompt_templates.title: Find a basic skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-skills to search for a skill that helps with PDF extraction. Summarize the best match and why it fits.

prompt_templates.title: Compare adjacent searches
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-skills for three related queries about frontend design. Pool the results and recommend one skill.

prompt_templates.title: Review safety signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-skills to search for deployment skills. Explain any caution or risky flags before recommending a candidate.

prompt_templates.title: Produce JSON for analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Run find-skills with JSON output for test automation skills, then summarize the top candidates by source and safety status.

output_examples.input: Find a skill for React performance work.
output_examples.output: The response names a primary skill, shows which registry found it, lists installs or stars, and explains why it matches React performance.

output_examples.input: Search for video generation skills with safety scanning.
output: A short source-health summary is shown.
Top candidates from each registry are listed.
Any risky scan flags are called out before a recommendation.

output_examples.input: Find an already installed skill for documentation work.
output_examples.output: The report highlights matching installed skills so the user can reuse one without installing another package.

best_practices: Run two or three adjacent queries for non-trivial needs before deciding.
Read the top candidate skill files before recommending or installing anything.
Treat risk badges as prompts for manual review, not final security decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not recommend a skill from metadata alone.
Do not treat match percentage as a quality score.
Do not install or run discovered skills without explicit user approval.

faq.question: Does this skill install other skills automatically?
faq.answer: No. It only searches and reports candidates. Installation remains a separate user-approved action.

faq.question: Which registries does it search?
faq.answer: It searches skills.sh, clawhub.ai, and GitHub repositories tagged with common agent skill topics.

faq.question: Does it require API keys?
faq.answer: No API keys are required. GitHub results depend on the local gh CLI being available.

faq.question: Is the security scan a full audit?
faq.answer: No. It is a heuristic scan for common risky patterns and should be followed by manual review.

faq.question: Can it detect installed skills?
faq.answer: It checks common local skill directories by folder name and marks matching results as installed.

faq.question: Why should I run adjacent queries?
faq.answer: Registries often index skill names more than intent, so related terms can surface stronger candidates.
